subject: Re: API response degradation Sep 14 — attribution & credit request
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@atlaspay.com>
To: jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: devops@atlaspay.com, support@atlaspay.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: API response degradation Sep 14 — request for attribution and credits

Hi Jordan,

We observed a visible degradation in your hosted inference API between 08:40–09:05 PDT yesterday. Customer-facing transactions were delayed or retried — our telemetry shows ~3.7% higher latency and a spike in 5xx errors for the payment tokenization route. This materially affected a subset of our checkouts for ~25 minutes.

Per our SLA (section 3.2, attached), we believe this qualifies for a partial uptime credit. We need Redwood to:
- Confirm the root cause (owning component vs third-party dependency).
- Share the calculation method you will use to apportion availability for this window (especially if a CDN/peering provider is involved).
- Provide the logs/probe evidence you relied on.

I’ve attached a short sample of error logs and our spike chart. Can we get a timeline and proposed credit apportionment by EOD? This incident impacted a scheduled promotion and has finance implications for our month-end.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Integrations — AtlasPay

Hi Samira — thanks for the heads up and for the artifacts.

We’re investigating now. Ben (cc’d) is pulling the probe and routing traces and will correlate with our edge telemetry. Initial ask: can you confirm whether the affected tokenization calls were routed to the same region (us-west-2) or spanned multiple regions? That helps us determine whether this is an edge peering issue or our internal path.

Tentative next steps:
- Ben will assemble a timeline and probe dump.
- I’ll run a quick SLA apportionment using our standard method (per your contract) and share a preliminary number.
- If this is due to a third-party CDN or upstream carrier, we’ll outline a proposed split and the evidence we’re using.

We’ll aim to get the preliminary findings by 5pm PT today.

Best,
Jordan Blake

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: API response degradation Sep 14 — request for attribution and credits

Hi Samira, Jordan —

I pulled the traces and probes for 08:30–09:20 PDT and cross-referenced:
- Our internal server metrics (controller and inference runtime) show no sustained CPU/GPU saturation.
- We observed a transient spike in TCP retransmits between our edge POP in SFO1 and the upstream CDN pop operated by CloudFjord at ~08:39–08:58 PDT. The spike aligns with the first customer reports.
- Our synthetic probes (global HTTP checks) indicate elevated tail latency to the same CDN pop during that window.

Why this matters for the SLA: our contract attributes availability first to the Redwood serving path; if a third-party CDN/peering provider is the proximate cause, standard apportionment policies call for partial exclusion of the internal path and a third-party adjustment. Practically, we do the following:
1) Define the incident window by when successful calls dropped vs baseline probes (08:39–08:58).
2) Count only requests that transited the affected edge POP(s) and classify them as: internal-only (routing stayed in our infra) vs external-proxied (handed to CloudFjord).
3) For external-proxied requests, apply a third-party attribution factor based on probe divergence and retransmit rate.

Attached: probe_latency_summary.csv (per-probe latencies by POP), a short snippet of tcp_retransmits.log, and the query I used to produce the request cohort.

Recommendation: preliminary apportionment suggests ~70% of the effective customer impact can be attributed to the CloudFjord CDN pop (i.e., Redwood internal path responsible for ~30% of the degradation). If AtlasPay accepts that split we can issue a corresponding partial SLA credit.

If you prefer, we can escalate to a manual apportionment review — Marissa is looped for approvals beyond formulaic splits.

- Ben
Senior Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: probe_latency_summary.csv (csv), tcp_retransmits.log (text)

Jordan / Ben —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and for sharing the probe CSV. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our edge logs show the same retransmit pattern for traffic that never left the us-west-2 region (all traffic seen by our load balancer headed to Redwood’s SFO1 endpoint). We can share full flow logs if that helps.
- AtlasPay’s legal team is focused on the SLA text: it expects Redwood to maintain availability for the public API, and third-party chain exceptions require clear evidence. Our position: given the business impact, we would prefer Redwood to take the credit calculation conservatively (i.e., at most a 25% third-party attribution).

Attached: a short sample of our flow logs and the signed-sla-excerpt.pdf that the procurement team retained. Can you run the apportionment with a 25% max third-party attribution and show the math? If Redwood can’t accept that cap we’ll need a manual review process and a short executive call.

Samira

Hi Samira — Jordan —

Thanks everyone for the data. I reviewed Ben’s probe analysis and AtlasPay’s flow samples. To be pragmatic and preserve the partnership, Redwood will:

- Accept a conservative apportionment for this incident: Redwood accepts 60% attribution for the outage window (08:39–08:58 PDT). That reflects our internal telemetry plus the probe divergence.
- Issue a partial SLA credit equal to 60% of the calculated downtime impact for the affected route for Sep 14. We will compute the credit using the standard SLA formula in your contract and apply it to your next billing cycle.
- Upload the final calculation and the supporting artifacts to the linked Jira ticket (INF-5821) and the HubSpot deal record.

If you need the explicit calculation steps in a spreadsheet format, Ben will produce that and I’ll sign off. If AtlasPay wants an executive call to walk through the math, I’m available tomorrow morning.

Jordan — please follow up with AtlasPay with the final credit amount and attach the calculation workbook.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
